title: Tejpal Singh v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.; Deepak Verma, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; officer to decide Samadhan Yojna or Clause 6.14 instalments; recovery stayed four weeks.
headnote: On a pumping-set consumer's writ against a post-disconnection arrears demand after an asserted Surcharge Samadhan Yojna deposit, the Allahabad High Court, without deciding entitlement, disposed of the petition with liberty to represent to the named officer. That officer must pass a speaking order on the settlement scheme and, if it does not apply, consider deposit of the balance in instalments under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within three weeks; recovery stayed for four weeks or until that decision.
facts: The petitioner held a 7.5 kW pumping-set connection. He admitted delayed bill payment and claimed to have deposited Rs 32,715 under a Surcharge Samadhan Yojna. The licensee demanded Rs 1,10,093 on 23 June 2021 and disconnected supply on 15 July 2021. It contended that the settlement sum was not deposited in time and that Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 permitted instalments. The petitioner offered to apply for instalments while recovery continued.

holding_units.topic: instalment of arrears after failed surcharge settlement
holding_units.holding: Without deciding whether the consumer was entitled to the Surcharge Samadhan Yojna or to restoration of a pumping-set supply disconnected for arrears, the Court disposed of the writ with liberty to represent to the named officer. That officer must decide by speaking order—giving reasons if the settlement scheme is inapplicable—and in the alternative consider deposit of the balance in instalments under Clause 6.14 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, within three weeks of communication. Recovery under the impugned demand remains in abeyance for four weeks or until that decision, whichever is earlier; amounts already deposited are to be taken into account.

principle_tags.application: Where a consumer's claim to a surcharge-settlement scheme is disputed and supply has been disconnected for arrears, the Court did not grant instalments itself but directed the named officer, if the scheme does not apply, to consider deposit of the balance under Clause 6.14 of the Supply Code, with a short stay of recovery pending that speaking order.

not_decided.point: Entitlement to the Surcharge Samadhan Yojna
not_decided.note: Left to a speaking order of respondent no. 3; reasons required if the benefit is refused.

not_decided.point: Deposit of the balance in Clause 6.14 instalments
not_decided.note: To be considered in the alternative if the settlement scheme does not apply; not granted on the writ.

not_decided.point: Restoration of the disconnected pumping-set supply
not_decided.note: Supply was disconnected on 15.07.2021; the Court stayed recovery only, without directing reconnection.
